entries.title: Psalms 37:1
segments:
PSALM XXXVII. 
 
  David exhorts to patience and confidence in God, ver. 1-8.   Shews the different state of the righteous and the wicked, ver. 9-40.   A psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. Fret not-Because they prosper in their wicked enterprizes.

entries.title: Psalms 37:5
segments: V. 5. Commit-All thy cares and business, and necessities, commend to God by fervent prayer.

entries.title: Psalms 37:6
segments: V. 6. Judgment-It shall be as visible to men, as the light of the sun, at noon-day.

entries.title: Psalms 37:7
segments: V. 7. Rest-Do not repine at his dealings, but quietly submit to his will, and wait for his help.

entries.title: Psalms 37:8
segments: V. 8. Fret not-Either against the sinner for his success; or against God.  Do evil-If grief arise in thee, take care that it do not transport thee to sin.

entries.title: Psalms 37:9
segments: V. 9. The earth-This for the most part was literally fulfilled in that state of the church.

entries.title: Psalms 37:10
segments: V. 10. Not be-He shall be dead and gone.  Diligently-Industriously seeking him.  His place-His place and estate, and glory.

entries.title: Psalms 37:11
segments: V. 11. But-Those who patiently bear God's afflicting hand, and meekly pass by injuries.  Peace-Partly of outward peace and prosperity, which God in his due time will give them: but principally of inward peace, in the sense of God's favour and the assurance of endless happiness.

entries.title: Psalms 37:13
segments: V. 13. His day-The day appointed by God for his punishment or destruction.

entries.title: Psalms 37:18
segments: V. 18. Knoweth-Observes with care and affection.  The days-All things which befal them, their dangers and fears, and suffering. For ever-To them and their seed for ever: and when they die their inheritance is not lost, but exchanged for one infinitely better.

entries.title: Psalms 37:20
segments: V. 20. Fat-Which in an instant melts before the fire.

entries.title: Psalms 37:23
segments: V. 23. Established-So that he shall not fall into mischief.

entries.title: Psalms 37:24
segments: V. 24. Fall-Into trouble.

entries.title: Psalms 37:25
segments: V. 25. Forsaken-These temporal promises, were more express to the Jews in the times of the Old Testament, than to Christians.

entries.title: Psalms 37:26
segments: V. 26. Blessed-Not only with spiritual, but with temporal blessings.

entries.title: Psalms 37:27
segments: V. 27. Dwell-Thou shalt dwell in the land, and afterwards in heaven.

entries.title: Psalms 37:30
segments: V. 30. The mouth-Having shewed, God's singular care over the righteous, he proceeds to give a character of them.  Judgment-Of God's judgment, word or law.

entries.title: Psalms 37:31
segments: V. 31. Heart-His thoughts, meditations and affections are fixed upon it.  Slide-Slide, or swerve, from the rule, from God's law.

entries.title: Psalms 37:35
segments: V. 35. Bay-tree-Which is continually green and flourishing even in winter.

entries.title: Psalms 37:36
segments: V. 36. Yet-He was gone in an instant.  But-There was no monument or remainder of him left.

entries.title: Psalms 37:37
segments: V. 37. Peace-Though he may meet with troubles in his way, yet all shall end well.

entries.title: Psalms 37:38
segments: V. 38. Together-All without exception.
